threats.title: Undetected onboard clock bias
threats.mechanism: GNSS or clock-disciplining faults introduce measurement timestamp errors that propagate into localisation, potentially exceeding horizontal accuracy requirements without triggering integrity alarms.

threats.title: Forged or misleading aircraft reports
threats.mechanism: Unauthenticated ADS-B self-reports permit false aircraft identities, positions, or trajectories to enter the observation chain and potentially influence association and integrity decisions.

threats.title: Compromised integrity-monitoring logic
threats.mechanism: Compromise or manipulation of integrity checks or cross-check logic suppresses discrepancy warnings or generates misleading integrity annotations that propagate to ATM.

threats.title: Compromised central processing platform
threats.mechanism: Host or virtualisation compromise enables manipulation of measurements, reference data, processing logic, integrity verdicts, or report delivery.

threats.title: Malicious or compromised software update
threats.mechanism: An unauthorised or compromised update introduces malicious firmware, altered thresholds, or weakened validation across payload and ground processing components.

threats.title: Ephemeris corruption causing systematic localisation error
threats.mechanism: Incorrect or maliciously modified orbit products distort satellite geometry and measurement predictions, biasing solutions and potentially undermining residual-based integrity checks.

threats.title: Integrity-threshold manipulation
threats.mechanism: Unauthorised changes to detection thresholds, time-conformance policy, or acceptance criteria cause hazardous solutions to pass or legitimate reports to be rejected.

threats.title: Telemetry manipulation through link compromise
threats.mechanism: Compromised communications alter, inject, reorder, or suppress relayed observations, degrading association, localisation, or the freshness and consistency of measurement sets.

threats.title: Malicious telecommand execution
threats.mechanism: Unauthorised or misused telecommands change payload operation, onboard software, timing configuration, or satellite availability.

threats.title: Key compromise across mission communications
threats.mechanism: Compromised cryptographic keys undermine the authenticity or confidentiality of protected commands and links, enabling further manipulation or disclosure.

threats.title: False aircraft observations from coordinated emitters
threats.mechanism: Coordinated unauthenticated emissions produce mutually plausible observations that may be associated as a genuine aircraft or distort an existing track.

threats.title: GNSS-dependent timing degradation
threats.mechanism: GNSS interference or misleading timing information degrades onboard clock discipline, while insufficient independent timing validation allows biased timestamps to enter observations.

threats.title: PTP time-transfer manipulation
threats.mechanism: Compromised or faulty time-transfer sources introduce offsets, asymmetry, or drift into satellite clock discipline, even where individual messages are cryptographically authenticated.

threats.title: Payload measurement extraction compromise
threats.mechanism: Faulty or compromised extraction firmware biases decoded fields or TOA, FOA, and AOA measurements, contaminating downstream localisation and integrity assessment.

threats.title: RF front-end interference or saturation
threats.mechanism: Interference, saturation, or degraded antenna performance reduces reception quality, distorts arrival measurements, or removes observations needed for adequate geometric observability.

threats.title: Satellite platform compromise
threats.mechanism: Compromise of flight software or the onboard computer enables payload disruption, measurement alteration, clock manipulation, or interruption of report relay.

threats.title: Ground-station command-path compromise
threats.mechanism: Compromise of ground-station modems, command infrastructure, or associated interfaces enables unauthorised commands or disrupts command and telemetry availability.

threats.title: Observable replay or freshness failure
threats.mechanism: Replayed, delayed, duplicated, or stale reports are accepted without adequate freshness and sequence validation, corrupting association or presenting outdated aircraft states.

threats.title: Measurement association poisoning
threats.mechanism: Ambiguous identities, coincident receptions, corrupted metadata, or inconsistent association logic combine observations from different transmissions or split observations of one aircraft.

threats.title: Solver or tracker state manipulation
threats.mechanism: Manipulated solver inputs, compromised tracking state, or faulty estimation logic create incorrect positions, persistent track drift, track swaps, or lost targets.

threats.title: Integrity-monitor false acceptance
threats.mechanism: Correlated errors, inadequate fault hypotheses, model mismatch, or incomplete residual testing permit an unsafe solution to pass as acceptable.

threats.title: Integrity-monitor false rejection
threats.mechanism: Overly conservative thresholds, faulty consistency assumptions, or manipulated inputs cause valid aircraft solutions to be rejected or labelled untrustworthy.

threats.title: Ephemeris or clock-state database tampering
threats.mechanism: Unauthorised database modification, stale records, or inconsistent versioning corrupts geometry and clock corrections used by localisation and integrity calculations.

threats.title: ASTERIX report alteration or misencoding
threats.mechanism: Incorrect or manipulated encoding, field mapping, integrity annotation, or message handling changes the meaning of surveillance reports delivered to ATM.

threats.title: Central processing resource exhaustion
threats.mechanism: Excessive, malformed, or unusually dense inputs exhaust processing, storage, or network resources and delay or interrupt surveillance outputs.

threats.title: Synchronisation policy compromise
threats.mechanism: Unauthorised or erroneous time-reference policy changes weaken clock acceptance, consistency checking, or recovery criteria and permit timing faults to propagate.

threats.title: Orbit-determination service compromise
threats.mechanism: Compromised orbit-determination infrastructure publishes incorrect or unauthorised ephemeris products that propagate into localisation reference data.

threats.title: Credential theft and privilege escalation
threats.mechanism: Stolen credentials, excessive privileges, or compromised remote access allow unauthorised control of management services, cryptographic material, or central processing systems.

threats.title: Sensitive mission data disclosure
threats.mechanism: Unauthorised access exposes keys, precise ephemerides, configurations, audit records, or non-public traffic that may enable subsequent attacks or compromise operational confidentiality.

threats.title: Insider misuse or supplier compromise
threats.mechanism: An authorised person or compromised supplier misuses legitimate access to change configurations, expose secrets, disable safeguards, or conceal unauthorised activity.

threats.title: Management network and audit-log compromise
threats.mechanism: Compromise of management workstations, remote access, or audit storage enables configuration changes, secret theft, persistence, or concealment of unauthorised operations.

threats.title: Surveillance feed interruption or degradation
threats.mechanism: Feed outages, stale delivery, capacity limitations, or interface failures prevent timely reception of surveillance reports or integrity annotations by ATM.

threats.title: ATM misinterpretation of integrity annotations
threats.mechanism: Ambiguous integrity semantics, inconsistent display behaviour, or operational misunderstanding causes controllers or downstream systems to treat unsafe or unavailable reports as trustworthy.

threats.title: Inter-satellite link availability loss
threats.mechanism: Crosslink outages, interference, routing faults, or terminal compromise prevent timely delivery of observations and reduce the number or distribution of usable measurements.

threats.title: Downlink and backhaul availability loss
threats.mechanism: Communication outages, interference, congestion, or infrastructure failure interrupt report delivery from satellites to the processing station.

threats.title: Satellite geometry degradation
threats.mechanism: Poor constellation geometry, antenna limitations, or loss of contributing satellites increases localisation uncertainty and reduces fault-detection capability even without malicious interference.

threats.title: Inadequate cryptographic attribution
threats.mechanism: Insufficient authenticated provenance, replay protection, or end-to-end integrity prevents reliable attribution of observation and command changes across trust boundaries.

threats.title: Insufficient fault independence across checks
threats.mechanism: The solver, integrity monitor, and ADS-B cross-check share assumptions or corrupted reference inputs, allowing correlated faults to evade nominally independent checks.

threats.title: Inadequate configuration provenance and rollback
threats.mechanism: Missing configuration provenance, version consistency, or safe rollback permits unreviewed changes or failed updates to persist across payload and ground components.

threats.title: RF measurement bias from environmental effects
threats.mechanism: Multipath, interference, receiver calibration drift, or angle-estimation errors bias observables and can create systematic localisation errors or false integrity alarms.

threats.title: Repudiation through insufficient audit evidence
threats.mechanism: Incomplete, mutable, or poorly correlated audit records prevent reliable attribution of privileged configuration changes, command issuance, and key-management actions.

threats.title: Incorrect aircraft identity or track association
threats.mechanism: Identity collisions, stale track state, or inconsistent ADS-B and independent localisation associations cause aircraft tracks to be merged, split, or assigned incorrect identities.

architecture_weaknesses: The unauthenticated ADS-B self-report is not an independent truth source; agreement with MLAT can be misleading when observations are manipulated or correlated.
The stated conversion from clock offset to range and horizontal error is simplified; actual error depends on measurement geometry, estimator behaviour, clock correlations, and observation selection.
W2 assumes universal detection of every requirement-breaching single-satellite bias in STRONG passes without specifying validated fault models, measurement availability, or monitor coverage.
W3 assumes a non-empty stealth window in WEAK passes without defining the detection function, uncertainty bounds, fault distributions, or empirical validation conditions.
W1 cites a literature-reported covert bias but does not establish transferability to the specific onboard clock architecture, disciplining logic, or operational environment.
The architecture does not explicitly define end-to-end report provenance, freshness guarantees, replay protection, or how authentication failures affect safety-related outputs.
The integrity monitor and cross-check may share solver inputs, ephemerides, clock states, and configuration, undermining their independence against common-mode faults.

Trust boundaries are incomplete or inconsistent: several critical assets have no boundary assigned, and the register does not fully specify redundancy, recovery behaviour, fail-safe states, or operational acceptance criteria.
overall: The dominant hazards are deceptive unauthenticated observations, timing and ephemeris errors, compromised integrity logic, and failures across command, update, and processing trust boundaries. The STRONG/WEAK distinction is a useful hypothesis, not an established guarantee: its validity requires explicit fault models, uncertainty analysis, and independent validation. Evidence ratings are conservative judgments, not a verified literature survey; E3 denotes analogous documented classes where system-specific evidence may be absent.
